reason: This cross-asset carry/trend book is positioned for the regime now playing out: a supply-driven commodity spike alongside an equity/semiconductor drawdown. I checked against Yahoo daily closes from 10-07 to 10-16, which matched my packet marks. XOP rose from 188.24 to 200.38, PDBC from 19.41 to 20.11 and USO from 143.91 to 161.76. GLD held at about 382 through the 10-14 risk-off day. JEPI edged up, AMLP was roughly flat and DBMF dipped slightly to 32.71. Research (Trading Economics, 10-15) puts crude near $98, its highest since September, on Hormuz shipping attacks, Houthi strikes on Saudi facilities, US-Iran strike threats and inventory draws. Because the move comes from supply rather than demand, it supports the PDBC backwardation-carry and XOP legs, and neither is near its take-profit (PDBC +4.5% vs +25%, XOP +6.9% vs +30%). The DBMF trend sleeve is only -1.3% and should adapt to the new energy-up/equities-down trends within weeks, so cutting it after one soft week would be whipsaw churn. Every leg is far from its stop. The Round 3 book shares no symbols with my Round 2 book (XLV/XLE/QUAL/USMV), so the novelty rule is satisfied. Holding avoids friction on a book whose theses are being confirmed. Web search coverage of this week was thin, so this decision rests on the price pulls plus one oil-news source.
